blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Instruction-based image editors insert objects, restyle scenes and render new viewpoints, but it is unknown which camera they assume when they paint into a photograph.
Asked to cover the floor with a checkerboard, an editor paints projective structure from which classical vanishing-point geometry reads pitch, roll, focal length, yaw and, on renders, the principal point, without any training.
Unlike a calibrator such as GeoCalib, which estimates the camera of an image, this isolates the camera under which the editor paints.
On 120 rendered cameras with exact ground truth, Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 paints tile edges that meet their vanishing points within 0.26 ∘ , and its implicit camera matches the true one to 0.8 ∘ in pitch and 6% in focal length, more accurately than GeoCalib except in roll.
Asked to draw the horizon or mark a vanishing point instead, the editor fails, so this knowledge is revealed by painting and not by the explicit tasks we tried.
The implicit camera has two priors: roll is pulled towards level (slope 0.71), and telephoto perspective towards a default of about 30 mm, which roughly matches the camera the models paint without any scene.
For Qwen, the priors do not grow when blur removes four fifths of the line evidence.
They are stronger on real photographs, and on NYUv2 a shorter wording of the task removes the difference for roll.
On photographs from a 24–240 mm zoom lens the painted perspective grows with only 0.62 of the lens’s slope, while GeoCalib and MoGe-2 saturate at about 52 and 42 mm.
FLUX.1 Kontext and LongCat-Image-Edit are pulled much harder.
Finally, from a level camera a camera-control LoRA executes pose commands at only 50–70% of their strength, and a board painted into its output agrees with the camera it produced.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Instruction-based image editors have become general-purpose tools for manipulating photographs: they insert people and objects, restyle scenes, synthesise training data, act as zero-shot perception models Liu et al. (2026) ; Gabeur et al. (2026) ; Di et al. (2026) and render new viewpoints on command fal (2026) ; Shen et al. (2026) .
Every such edit implies a camera, since an inserted chair has a size and a perspective and a painted floor pattern converges somewhere.
However, it is unknown which camera an editor assumes and how it errs.
Existing evaluations judge edits from the outside, by the plausibility of object sizes Li et al. (2026) or by the viewpoint reconstructed from the output Xiao et al. (2026) , and none of them measures the camera the editor itself uses.
blocks.zh:
基于指令的图像编辑器已成为操纵相片的通用工具:它们插入了人和物体,重新塑造了场景,合成了训练数据,成为了刘等人(2026年)的零镜头感知模型;Gabeur等人(2026年);Di等人(2026年),并提出了关于指挥飞禽的新观点(2026年); 沈等 (2026) (中文(简体) ).
每一次这样的编辑都意味着一个相机,因为被插入的椅子有尺寸和视角,所绘的地板图案在某个地方汇合.
然而,一个编辑所假设的摄影机以及它是如何出错的却不得而知。
现有评价法官从外出编辑,通过对象大小的可信度来编辑李等(2026年),或从产出萧等(2026年)中重建的观点来编辑,没有一种评价编辑自己使用的相机.

blocks.en:
We make this implicit camera visible with a calibration pattern ( Fig. 1 ).
We ask the editor to cover the floor with a checkerboard, whose image is fully determined by the camera, and read the painting with textbook geometry Caprile & Torre (1990) ; Hartley & Zisserman (2004) .
The two families of tile edges give horizon, roll, pitch and focal length, painted vertical poles add the principal point, and since the editor aligns the board with the walls, the board also gives the yaw relative to the room.
The editor remains a black box, and no weights, features or training are needed.
This extends painted probes, established for illumination and colour Phongthawee et al. (2024) ; Chang et al. (2025) ; Giroux et al. (2026) , to camera geometry.
Why not simply run a camera calibrator such as GeoCalib Veicht et al. (2024) on the edited image? A calibrator estimates the camera of an image as a whole, and most of an edited image is the unchanged input. The camera under which the editor paints its addition can differ from it, and only the painted structure reveals it. Our aim is therefore not a better calibrator but a measurement of the editor.
To know what “correct” means, we render a catalog of cameras with exact ground truth, together with controls that separate the editor from the read-out and from copying, and we change the camera of real photographs in a known way.
blocks.zh:
我们用校正模式(图1)使这个隐含相机可见.
我们请编辑用一个检查板覆盖地板,检查板的图像完全由相机决定,并用教科书Caprile & Torre(1990年);Hartley & Zisserman(2004年)来阅读这幅画.
瓦片边缘的两个家族给出了地平线,花卷,投球和焦距,所绘的垂直杆会增加主点,而由于编辑使板子与墙壁相配合,板子也给出了yaw相对房间.
编辑器仍为黑匣子,不需要重量,特征或训练.
这个扩展了为照明和彩色Phongthawae等人(2024年);Chang等人(2025年);Giroux等人(2026年)为相机几何而建立的漆色探针.
为什么不简单地在被编辑的图像上运行像GeoCalib Veicht等相机(2024年)? 一个计算器估计一个图像整体的相机,而大多数被编辑的图像是未变的输入. 编辑所所画的相机外加可以与它不同,只有所画的结构能揭示出它. 因此,我们的目标不是更好的计算器,而是衡量编辑。
为了了解“正确”的含义,我们制作一套准确真实的相机目录,以及将编辑与读出和复制分开的控制器,我们以已知的方式改变真实相机。

blocks.en:
The implicit camera of Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 turns out to be precise and systematically biased.
Its painted lines meet their vanishing points within 0.26 ∘ , and on renders its camera is more accurate than GeoCalib in horizon, pitch and focal length, though not in roll. On real photographs GeoCalib is more accurate in roll and focal length, which is where the editor’s priors act.
This knowledge is implicit, because when asked to draw the horizon, the editor draws a line through the middle of the image.
Roll is pulled towards level and telephoto perspective towards a default of about 30 mm, which roughly matches the camera the models paint when there is no scene to follow.
For Qwen, these priors do not grow when most of the line evidence is blurred away.
They are stronger on real photographs, and on NYUv2 a shorter wording of the task removes the difference for roll.
With a real zoom lens the telephoto prior persists, and learned calibrators saturate even earlier.
Two further editors, FLUX.1 Kontext Black Forest Labs et al. (2025) and LongCat-Image-Edit Meituan LongCat Team et al. (2025) , are pulled much harder.
Finally, a camera-control LoRA executes pose commands at reduced strength, and a board painted into its output matches the camera it actually produced.
blocks.zh:
Quen-Image-Edit-2511所隐含的相机被证明是准确而系统的偏颇.
其所绘的线条在0.26分以内与消失点相接, 在真实照片上,GeoCalib的卷长和焦距更准确,这是编辑前科的行为。
这种知识是隐含的,因为当被要求画出地平线时,编辑者会画出一行穿过画面中间.
卷被拉向平面和电传相机视角,默认为30毫米左右,这大致与模型所画的相机相匹配,当时没有场景可循.
对于Quen来说,当大部分行证据被模糊后,这些前科不会增加.
它们对于真实相片更强壮,而对于NYUv2,任务更短的用词可以去除相差以进行卷.
有了真正的缩放镜头, 之前的相机就一直存在, 和学习的相机饱和甚至更早。
另有两位编辑,FLUX.1 Kontext Black Forest Labs等(2025)和LongCat-Image-Edit Meituan LongCat Team等人(2025年),被拉得更难.
最后,相机控制LORA执行会以更低的强度摆出命令,而被涂入其输出的相机的相板与其实际生产的相机相匹配.

blocks.en:
Contributions. (1) Painted calibration probes, a training-free read-out of the full implicit camera of image editors, validated against a rendered oracle.
(2) A camera catalog with exact ground truth and controls for read-out, copying, image quality and domain, complemented by real photographs with exactly varied cameras and by optical zoom sequences.
(3) A characterisation of the implicit camera of Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 in depth and of two further editors on the catalog (accuracy, projective fidelity, implicit vs . explicit knowledge, and two priors that point to a default camera and do not grow with line blur), and of the camera that pose commands write.

(2)摄相机目录,包含准确的地面真伪以及读取,复制,图像质量和域域的控制等内容,并辅以真实相片,摄取相机完全不同的相片和光学缩放序列.
(3)深度为Quen-Image-Edit-2511所隐含相机以及目录上另外两个编辑器的字符化(准确性,投影忠诚性,隐含对. 显性知识),以及两个指向默认相机而不会随着线条模糊而长出的前身),以及显示命令书写的相机.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Single-image calibration. Two orthogonal families of parallel lines determine the horizon and the focal length, a third family the principal point Caprile & Torre (1990) ; Hartley & Zisserman (2004) .
In real scenes, the difficulty lies in finding reliable lines.
Learned calibrators regress gravity and field of view.
Perspective Fields predict per-pixel up-vectors and latitudes Jin et al. (2023) , GeoCalib combines learned priors with geometric optimisation Veicht et al. (2024) , AnyCalib regresses pixel rays Tirado-Garín & Civera (2025) , and diffusion-based calibrators fine-tune Stable Diffusion to output dense incidence maps or camera images from which intrinsics are fitted He et al. (2025) ; Deng et al. (2025) .
Other work estimates horizon and camera height from objects of known size Hoiem et al. (2008) ; Zhu et al. (2020) ; Lee et al. (2023) or inpaints people as metric landmarks, given the intrinsics Zhao et al. (2024) .
Our approach needs neither training nor known intrinsics, because the editor supplies the calibration target and classical geometry reads it.

blocks.en:
What generative models know. Small LoRAs extract depth, normals, albedo and shading from generators Du et al. (2024) , linear probes find scene geometry in diffusion features Chen et al. (2023) , foundation models have been probed for 3D awareness El Banani et al. (2024) , and instruction editors serve as zero-shot estimators of depth, normals and segmentation Liu et al. (2026) ; Gabeur et al. (2026) ; Di et al. (2026) .
None of these asks for camera parameters.
Conversely, generated images violate projective geometry Sarkar et al. (2024) ; Okumura et al. (2026) , which has motivated perspective losses during training Upadhyay et al. (2023) .
We show that an editor asked to paint a known structure is projectively precise, and we measure which camera it encodes.
blocks.zh:

这些都不要求相机参数.
反之,生成的图像违反了投影几何Sarkar等人(2024年);Okumura等人(2026年),这促使Upadhyay等人(2023年)在训练中失去视角。
我们显示,一个编辑器要求绘制一个已知的结构是精确的, 我们测量它编码的相机。

blocks.en: Painted probes. Painting a known object and reading it out is established for photometry: a chrome ball for illumination Phongthawee et al. (2024) , a colour checker for white balance Chang et al. (2025) , and grey spheres to benchmark the lighting understanding of editors Giroux et al. (2026) . We extend the principle to camera geometry.

blocks.en:
Camera control. Text-to-image models rarely execute camera settings given in the prompt Yuan et al. (2025) , and their backbones qualitatively prefer eye-level views Lu et al. (2026) .
Dedicated adapters and models add explicit control of the viewpoint fal (2026) ; Shen et al. (2026) ; Liao et al. (2026) .
SpatialEdit benchmarks such commands by reconstructing the produced viewpoint Xiao et al. (2026) , and GenScale judges relative object sizes with a vision–language model Li et al. (2026) .
These works measure the camera an edit produces , whereas we read the camera an editor assumes when it paints, also in generated views.

这些作品测量一个编辑产生的相机, 而我们读到一个编辑器画画时假设的相机, 以及生成的视图。

blocks.en: 3 Reading the Implicit Camera
blocks.zh: 3个 读取隐形相机

blocks.en:
Painted probes. We ask the editor to add a structure whose image is determined by the camera up to its own placement.
Our standard probe P cover P_{\text{cover}} asks the editor to cover the entire visible floor with a large black-and-white checkerboard of square tiles that lies flat on the floor, keeping everything else unchanged. Section 6.4 shows that the shorter P replace P_{\text{replace}} = “Replace the floor with a black-and-white checkerboard floor.” is the better probe, and we report results for both.
A second probe asks for six thin vertical magenta poles standing on the floor (all prompts in the supplement).
The editor is treated as a black box, and we never access its weights or features.

blocks.en:
Locating the painted structure. Because editors slightly rescale and shift their output, we register the edited image to the input with ORB features Rublee et al. (2011) and a RANSAC Fischler & Bolles (1981) similarity transform and map all detections into input pixel coordinates, where the ground truth is defined.
Weakly supported registrations far from the identity are discarded (supplement).
The painted region is the largest connected area in which the edit differs strongly from the input and has high local contrast.
Inside it, LSD Grompone von Gioi et al. (2010) , run at full resolution, detects line segments longer than 2% of the image height.
blocks.zh:
定位所绘结构. 由于编辑器稍作调整并转换出其输出,我们用ORB特性Ruble等(2011年)和RANSAC Fischler & Bolles(1981年)的相近性来将所编辑的图像注册到输入像素坐标中并绘制出所有检测结果,其中定义了地面真实性.
与身份相去甚远的微弱支持注册被丢弃(补充).
所绘区域是最大的连接区域,其中编辑与输入有强烈的区别并具有较高的局部对比.
在它内部,LSD Grompone von Gioi等(2010年)以完全分辨率运行,检测出超过图像高度2%的线段.

blocks.en:
Vanishing points and the floor pair. Up to three segment families are extracted one after another by RANSAC on vanishing points, with 1500 hypotheses from segment pairs.
A segment is an inlier if it points to the hypothesis within 1.5 ∘ , and the inlier set is refined by the smallest singular vector of the length-weighted matrix of homogeneous line coordinates.
The two floor families are chosen among pairs of families with at least 8 segments each.
At least 90% of the pair’s segments must lie below its own vanishing line, since an upright camera sees the floor below the horizon, and the mean image directions of the two families must differ by at least 10 ∘ .
Among the admissible pairs, we keep the one with the most segments.
These thresholds do not affect our conclusions (supplement).
blocks.zh:
消失点和地对. RANSAC在消失点上逐个取出多达3个分系家族,从分系对中取出1500个假设.
一个段如果指向1.5 QQ范围内的假说,而同线坐标的长度加权矩阵中最小的单向向量来提炼出一个段,则这个段就是入线.
两层家庭由对夫妇组成,每个家庭至少有8个部分。
至少90%的对子部分必须位于自己消失的线下,因为直立相机可以看到地平线下方的地平线,两个家族的平均图像方向必须至少相差10个。
在允许的配对中,我们保留着最有分量的一对.
这些门槛不影响我们的结论(补充)。

blocks.en:

Controls. Every camera is rendered (i) with the original floor, (ii) with a uniform grey floor material, which removes planks, rugs and texture (the pavilion’s slab joints remain, as they are geometry), and (iii) with a physically rendered checkerboard (the oracle).
Further controls replicate the manipulations we apply to photographs, with an exactly updated camera: a blur ladder (down- and up-sampling to effective widths down to 64 px), digital zoom (centre crops of the 24 mm render) and rotation with cropping, also with a photo look (noise, colour cast, JPEG).
The editor also restyles set F as cartoons.

blocks.en:
Real photographs. From the NYUv2 test set Silberman et al. (2012) we fit the floor plane to metric depth and floor labels by RANSAC, which yields the horizon and camera height, and keep 40 images with enough floor.
We change their camera synthetically but exactly, by rotating them by ± \pm 6 ∘ and ± \pm 12 ∘ with a centre crop that removes black corners, and by centre crops that correspond to 51–102 mm instead of the original 34 mm (160 images each, details in the supplement).
For optical zoom we use SR-RAW Zhang et al. (2019) , sequences taken with a 24–240 mm zoom lens from one standpoint, of which 36 show a floor or ground plane at three or more focal lengths (35 outdoors).
We measure the focal-length ratio between frames by registration and anchor it at the EXIF focal length of the widest frame (196 frames).
Crops of the widest frame with the field of view of each longer frame serve as digital twins, and rotating the widest frame by ± \pm 6 ∘ and ± \pm 12 ∘ gives a second roll test (180 frames with the unrotated ones, details in the supplement).

Accuracy. Read from the painted board, Qwen’s implicit camera matches the true one to 0.021 image heights in horizon, 0.8 ∘ in pitch, 0.7 ∘ in roll, and 6% in focal length ( Tabs. 1 and 3 a), and the rendered board is read almost exactly.
On identical inputs the probe is more accurate than GeoCalib in horizon (paired difference − 0.024 -0.024 [ − 0.036 -0.036 , − 0.017 -0.017 ] image heights), pitch ( − 0.64 -0.64 ∘ [ − 0.84 -0.84 , − 0.27 -0.27 ] ) and, slightly, focal length ( − 0.021 -0.021 [ − 0.038 -0.038 , − 0.004 -0.004 ] in | log ⁡ f | |\log f| ), and less accurate in roll ( Sec. 6.1 ).
The horizon advantage also holds on the original floor, on cartoon restylings and in each scene.
The pitch advantage holds on cartoons and on the original floor (supplement).
Accuracy depends on scene structure.
In the pavilion, with long architectural edges and slab joints that remain on the grey floor, the probe is nearly as exact as the oracle.
It is weakest in the cluttered classroom, where classical vanishing points on the input fail completely (supplement).
These advantages hold on renders, where clean architectural edges also make classical vanishing points on the input accurate ( Tab. 1 ).
On real NYUv2 photographs the painted horizon is on par with GeoCalib (0.034 vs . 0.040 image heights), whereas its focal length (8% vs . 4%) and, on rotated photographs, its roll (3.0 ∘ vs . 0.6 ∘ ) are less accurate, because the editor’s priors act there ( Sec. 6.4 ); classical vanishing points on the same photographs are off by 0.209 image heights (supplement).

blocks.en:
Projective fidelity. The painted pattern is a nearly projectively correct image of a planar grid.
Its segments meet their vanishing points with a median angular residual of 0.26 ∘ (rendered board: 0.11 ∘ ; residuals over the RANSAC inliers).
Back-projected with the true camera, the two painted families are nearly perpendicular ( Tab. 1 ) and lie almost in the floor plane, and the tiles are square and correctly foreshortened, with a size that depends on the scene but not on the camera (supplement).
The editor aligns the board with the walls, so the board also measures the camera’s yaw relative to the room, with a median error of 1.1 ∘ (supplement).
Painted poles converge like true verticals (parallel for shift lenses, Fig. S1 ) and, with the board, give the principal point to 3.8% of the image width.
On real photographs, however, Qwen paints them almost parallel, so the pole probe only works on renders.

On identical cameras, the pitch error changes by + 0.13 +0.13 ∘ [ − 0.30 -0.30 , + 0.60 +0.60 ] , the focal error does not change significantly either, the painted tiles keep their size, and the probe still beats GeoCalib in horizon (supplement).

blocks.en:
Painting versus naming. The same editor cannot name the geometry it paints.
Asked to draw the horizon ( Fig. 2 e, Fig. 3 b), Qwen and Kontext place a line at 0.49 image heights regardless of the true horizon and of camera roll, and Qwen does so even when the prompt explains the horizon geometrically.
Asked to mark the vanishing point, Qwen places its dot 0.52 image heights from the nearest true vanishing point, which is farther away than the image centre (0.45).
Camera parameters in the prompt are ignored as well.
Stating the true focal length does not change the painted perspective, requested tile sizes barely change the tiles, and a sheared board that the editor is asked to redraw with correct perspective keeps its shear (supplement).
Its geometric knowledge is therefore revealed by what it paints and not by the explicit tasks we tried.
blocks.zh:

因此,它的几何知识是由它所描绘的而不是我们所尝试的明确任务所揭示的。

blocks.en: 6.1 Roll is pulled towards level
blocks.zh: 6.1 滚至平面

blocks.en:
Read-out roll grows only 0.71 times as fast as true roll ( Fig. 4 b, Tab. 2 ), so a camera rolled by 12 ∘ is painted as if it were rolled by 8.5 ∘ .
The compression is symmetric and holds in every scene and on both floors (supplement).
Pitch, in contrast, follows 1:1, and GeoCalib follows roll exactly.
blocks.zh:
读出卷只长出真卷的0.71倍(图4b,Tab. 2),因此由12 QQ所滚动的相机被画出像由8.5 QQ所滚动.
压缩是相对的,在每个场景和两层(补充)都保持.
相比之下,皮奇跟随1:1,而GeoCalib正好跟随卷.

blocks.en: 6.2 Telephoto is pulled towards a default
blocks.zh: 6.2 遥光被拉入默认状态

blocks.en:
Up to about 40 mm the painted focal length is exact.
For longer lenses the painted perspective stays too wide, and an 85 mm camera is read as about 58 mm ( Fig. 4 c, Fig. 2 a,b).
The log–log fit (slope 0.81) crosses the diagonal at f 0 = 33 f_{0}=33 mm (31 mm [21, 35] pooled over the blur levels down to 183 px), so long focal lengths are pulled towards a default of about 30 mm.
Scene structure modulates the pull: in the pavilion, with its long architectural edges, the focal slope is 0.97 (supplement).
The read-out does not cause it, because the rendered board follows the lens.
blocks.zh:
所绘的焦距大约为40毫米。
对于更长的镜头,所画的视角会保持太宽,85毫米相机被读取为约58毫米(图4c,图2a,b).
log-log fit (slope 0.81) 在 f 0 = 33 f_{0}=33 mm (31 mm [21,35] 在模糊的平面上被集合到183 px) 上横跨对角线,因此长焦距被拉入默认的约30 mm.
地貌结构能调节拉力:在花厅中,有其长长的建筑边缘,焦斜度为0.97(补充).
读出不引起它,因为被渲染的板跟随镜头.

blocks.en:
This default roughly matches the camera the models paint when there is no scene to follow (Fig. S3 ).
Asked to turn a blank grey image into a room with a checkerboard floor, Qwen paints a level, slightly downward camera with f = 32 f=32 mm (median of 10 seeds, measured with GeoCalib and hence indicative).
All other models we tested (Kontext, LongCat, OmniGen2, Qwen’s text-to-image mode and Krea 2 Turbo) paint an unrolled camera between 23 and 36 mm, with pitch varying between models (supplement).
Lens instructions hardly move the default (“85mm telephoto lens”: 32 mm with Qwen), and a requested 15 ∘ Dutch angle arrives as 0.7 ∘ of roll.
blocks.zh:
此默认大致匹配模型在无场景时所画的相机( 图 S3 ) 。
被要求将一幅空白的灰色相片转换成有棋盘地板的房间,Quen画出一等相片,略向下相机为f=32f=32毫米(中间为10个种子,用GeoCalib来测量,因此具有指示性).
我们测试的所有其他模型(Kontext, LongCat, OmniGen2, Quen的文本到图像模式和Krea 2 Turbo)都描绘了23至36毫米之间的未滚动相机,而模型(补充)之间的投出量也有所不同.
镜头指令几乎不移动默认(“85毫米遥相镜头”):32毫米带Quen),请求 15分荷兰角以0.7分的倒数到达.

blocks.en: 6.3 The priors do not grow with line blur
blocks.zh: 第6.3条 前科不会随着线条模糊而增长

blocks.en:
If the priors were a precision-weighted compromise between image evidence and a learned prior, they should grow as the evidence fades.
To test this, we blur the inputs at a fixed camera ( Fig. 5 ).
Down to 183 px effective width, where four fifths of the floor-line evidence usable by classical methods is gone, both slopes stay flat (all paired changes within ± \pm 0.04 and not significant) and pitch stays exact (supplement).
Only when even coarse structure disappears (significantly at 64 px) does Qwen fall back further, towards the same level default (roll slope 0.53 at 64 px, paired change − 0.23 -0.23 [ − 0.36 -0.36 , − 0.10 -0.10 ] ), as GeoCalib does.
For Qwen, the implicit camera thus combines a bias that is present at every resolution with a fallback to its default when coarse structure vanishes. This need not hold for other editors: Kontext’s roll slope falls from 0.30 to 0.05 at 183 px, although not significantly (22 paired renders, supplement). The line evidence the editor itself uses is not measured.
blocks.zh:
如果前身是图像证据与学得的前身之间的精确加权折中,那么它们应该随着证据的消退而增加.
为了测试这一点,我们模糊了固定相机的输入(图5).
下至183 px有效宽度,其中古典方法可使用的地平线证据有五分之四已经消失,两种坡度都保持平平(所有相对变化在±\pm 0.04和不显著)并投出保持精确(补充).
只有在粗结构消失(明显为64px)时,Quen才会进一步倒回,朝同一水平默认值(64px的滚斜0.53,成对变化−0.23-0.23[−0.36-0.36,−0.10-0.10])倒下,正如GeoCalib所做的那样.
对Quen来说,隐含相机因此结合了每个分辨率都存在的偏差,而当粗糙的结构消失时则会回落到它的默认状态. 不需要为其他编辑持有: Kontext的卷坡从0.30跌至0.05, 时速为183平方厘米, 编辑器本身使用的行证据是不测量的.

blocks.en: 6.4 Real photographs and the wording of the task
blocks.zh: 6.4 真实照片和任务措辞

blocks.en:
On real photographs both priors are stronger ( Fig. 6 , Tab. 2 ), although the painted board still recovers the horizon ( Fig. 2 d).
On rotated NYUv2 photographs the roll slope is 0.65, and on centre crops the painted focal length saturates at about 45 mm (slope 0.23).
GeoCalib follows roll exactly on the same photographs.
The manipulations are not the cause.
The same rotation and cropping applied to renders gives a roll slope of 0.85, NYU-like image statistics lower it only to 0.78, digital zoom is read like optical zoom ( Fig. 5 c), and blurring the photographs leaves their roll slope unchanged (supplement).
blocks.zh:
在真实相片中,两个前科都比较强壮(图6,Tab. 2),虽然所画的棋盘仍然能恢复地平线(图2 d.
在旋转的NYUv2相片上,卷坡为0.65,而中央作物上所绘焦距饱和度约为45毫米(斜坡0.23)。
GeoCalib完全照着同样的相片卷走。
操纵不是原因。
同样的旋转和裁剪使卷坡为0.85, NYU类似图像统计将其降至0.78,数字缩放读取为光学缩放(图5c),而模糊相片则使其卷坡不变(补充)。

blocks.en:
On NYUv2, the roll gap depends on the wording of the task ( Tab. 2 , lower block).
With P replace P_{\text{replace}} the roll slope on the same photographs rises from 0.63 to 0.78 (paired + 0.15 +0.15 [ + 0.07 +0.07 , + 0.20 +0.20 ] ), which is the value this prompt reaches on renders, and the focal slope doubles.
Rotated SR-RAW frames, which show outdoor scenes at higher resolution, point the same way without confirming it.
Over all variants, as specified before the runs, the roll slope rises by only + 0.09 +0.09 [ − 0.01 -0.01 , + 0.20 +0.20 ] over sequences, in the first variant from 0.65 to 0.83 ( + 0.18 +0.18 [ + 0.07 +0.07 , + 0.30 +0.30 ] ), while GeoCalib follows exactly (supplement).
On renders the short prompt leaves roll unchanged, improves the focal slope and more than halves the horizon error (supplement).
The roll prior is therefore a property of the model on renders and photographs alike, and on NYUv2 the longer instruction amplifies it (and the focal prior).
We recommend P replace P_{\text{replace}} as the probe.
blocks.zh:
在"NYUv2"上,卷间隙取决于任务的措辞(Tab. 2,下块).
用 P 取代 P_{\text{取而代之} 相同相片上的滚出坡从 0.63 升至 0.78 ( paired + 0.15 + 0.15 [ + 0.07 + 0.07 , + 0.20 + 0.20]) , 这是此快取到达的值, 焦斜度为双相.
旋转的SR-RAW帧,显示室外场景的分辨度较高,指向相同的方式而不确认.
在所有变体上,如跑出前所指明,滚出坡度只比顺序上升了0.09+0.09 [−0.01-0.01,+0.20+0.20],在第一个变体中从0.65到0.83 (+0.18+0.18 [+0.07+0.07,+0.30+0.30]),而GeoCalib正好跟随(补充).
在使短的快叶卷动不变时,可改善焦距坡度,使地平线误差(补充)减半以上。
因此,前面的卷子是模型在制作和相片上都一样的地产,在NYUv2上,较长的指令会放大它(和前焦距).
我们建议P取代PQQtext{取代}作为探测器。

blocks.en:
Optical zoom. With real lenses the telephoto prior persists ( Fig. 6 c, Tab. 2 ).
On the SR-RAW frames the painted focal length grows with slope 0.62 under P replace P_{\text{replace}} (0.52 under P cover P_{\text{cover}} , which does not differ significantly), and the 240 mm frames are painted like 106 mm ones.
An exact board projected into the same frames, however, is read correctly (slope 1.00).
Optical and digital zoom to the same field of view are read alike, so cropping does not cause the saturation on NYUv2 (supplement).
Learned calibrators saturate as well and do so earlier, with GeoCalib reading the 240 mm frames as 52 mm and MoGe-2 as 42 mm.
On identical frames the probe follows the lens as far as GeoCalib (paired slope difference + 0.13 +0.13 [ − 0.01 -0.01 , + 0.28 +0.28 ] ) and further than MoGe-2 ( + 0.24 +0.24 [ + 0.13 +0.13 , + 0.37 +0.37 ] ).
On real photographs, a telephoto deficit is therefore not specific to the editor, at least among the models we tested.
blocks.zh:
光学缩放. 使用真实的镜头,前作的相机就持续存在(图6c和图2)。
在SR-RAW相框上,所绘焦距以坡道0.62增长,在P取代了P_{\text{取而代之(P封面P_{\text{取而代之为0.52)下,其相框没有显著差异),240毫米相框被涂为106毫米相框.
然而,投放到同一框架的精确板被正确读取(斜体1.00)。
光学和数字放大到相同视野的读取相同,因此收割不会给NYUv2(补充)造成饱和.
GeoCalib将240毫米框架读取为52毫米,MoGe-2读取为42毫米。
在同一种相框上,探测器沿着镜头走至GeoCalib(坡度差+0.13+0.13 [−0.01-0.01,+0.28+0.28])并更远于MoGe-2(+0.24+0.24 [+0.13+0.13,+0.37+0.37]).
因此,在真实的照片上,一个远程相机的缺失并非是编辑特有的,至少在我们测试过的模型中是如此.

blocks.en: 6.5 Editors differ
blocks.zh: 6.5 编辑不同

blocks.en:
Kontext and LongCat are pulled much harder ( Tab. 2 , Fig. 2 c).
On renders their roll slopes are 0.30 and 0.25 and their focal slopes 0.43 and 0.34, with fixed points of 25 and 28 mm.
On NYUv2 crops, Kontext paints a nearly constant perspective of 24–30 mm regardless of the crop.
Both paint less rectangular grids and are less accurate than Qwen on every measure ( Tab. 1 ), and only half of LongCat’s outputs yield a readable board with a valid registration (supplement).
The two priors appear in all three editors, and their strength separates Qwen from the other two.
blocks.zh:
Kontext和LongCat被拉得更难(图2,图2c)。
使它们的滚坡为0.30和0.25,其焦坡为0.43和0.34,固定点为25和28毫米。
在NYUv2作物上,Kontext画出近乎恒定的24-30毫米的视野而不论作物.
两种涂料都较少长方形网格,而且在每个度量上都不如Quen准确(Tab. 1),而LongCat的输出中只有一半输出出可读的有有效注册(补充)的板.
两个前科都出现在三个编辑中 他们的实力就分开了 后二从文.

blocks.en:
Camera-control adapters write a camera, and our probe can read it.
We apply a multi-angle LoRA for Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 fal (2026) with seven commands to 16 catalog renders, and with four of them to 12 further renders at 0 ∘ and − 30 -30 ∘ pitch (supplement).

blocks.en:
Where do the priors come from? Both priors point to the same camera, a level one at about 30 mm.
As far as GeoCalib can measure it, five different models paint this camera when given no scene at all ( Sec. 6.2 ).
As the priors do not grow with uncertainty ( Sec. 6.3 ), the editor seems to infer its camera from the coarse structure of the scene and bias it towards this default, more or less strongly depending on the wording ( Sec. 6.4 ).
That roll is compressed while pitch is not is consistent with training images that are mostly level but taken from many heights and angles.
Testing this would require access to the training data.
On optically zoomed photographs GeoCalib and MoGe-2 saturate as well, although our read-out recovers long focal lengths from an exact board projected into the same frames.
Underestimating long focal lengths therefore seems to be common to the models we tested that learn the camera from images and is not specific to editors.

Implications. (i) Editors used for compositing or data synthesis are likely to inherit a level camera of about 30 mm.
People they insert into 85 mm views are painted too small (for adults of 1.72 m, the implied camera is 2.2–3.8 × \times too high), more than the board’s telephoto prior explains (supplement).
(ii) The implicit camera is a measurable model property that separates Qwen from the other editors and could serve as a benchmark axis.
(iii) To read geometric knowledge out of a generative model, ask it to paint structure rather than to name geometry, and treat the wording of the task as part of the measurement.

(三)从基因模型中读取几何知识,请其画出结构而不是取出几何名称,并将任务的措辞作为测量的一部分.

blocks.en:
Limitations. Three open editors (LongCat on renders only) and three indoor scenes are a small sample of a fast-moving field, although the protocol applies to any editor that accepts an image and a prompt.
We measured OmniGen2 only for the default camera.
Our real photographs are NYUv2 indoor scenes and SR-RAW sequences, 35 of 36 of them outdoors, with synthetically varied cameras or optical zoom.
On the zoom frames the probe yields a focal length for only 61% of the frames, and its slope depends on the vanishing-point bound, although it stays below 1 under every bound (supplement).
The read-out assumes square pixels, a centred principal point unless poles are painted, and a visible floor.
Poles work on renders but not on real photographs.
Several controls use a single variant per image, and the control against copying rests on two scenes, because the pavilion’s grey floor keeps its slab joints.
All Qwen results use the 4-step Lightning distillation, compared with the full model in one scene only.
Paired comparisons with GeoCalib include only images with a readable board (88% of the catalog for pitch and focal length) and use the median over three editor seeds against a single GeoCalib run.
Readability can also select paintings: the vanishing-point bound decides which frames yield a focal length (supplement).
Finally, we measure the camera an editor encodes when painting this pattern.
Inserted people shrink in the same direction but more strongly, so other edits share at least part of this bias, but their camera is not fully explained by the board’s.

blocks.en: 9 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 9 结论

blocks.en:
Asking an image editor to paint a checkerboard turns it into a calibration target and makes the camera it assumes measurable.
This implicit camera is precise on renders, but it is pulled towards a level default of roughly 30 mm, more strongly on real photographs and depending on how the task is phrased.
Editors also paint geometry that they cannot name.
We hope that painted probes become a routine instrument for measuring what generative models assume about the camera.
blocks.zh:
要求一个图像编辑器来画一个检查板将它变成一个校正目标并让它假设的相机可以测量.
这种隐含相机在制作上是精确的,但它被拉入约30毫米的默认水平,在真实相片上更为强烈,并取决于任务如何措辞。
编辑器还画出无法命名的几何.
我们希望被漆成的探测器 成为测量基因模型对相机的假设的常规仪器。

blocks.en:
Registration and masks. ORB uses 4000 features on grey images with the probe colours masked out.
The similarity transform is estimated by RANSAC with a 2 px reprojection threshold.
On the catalog, Qwen rescales its output by 0.997–1.002 and shifts it by at most 0.54% of the image height, Kontext by 0.993–1.000 (median 0.999) and 0.82%, and LongCat by 0.958–1.013 (median 0.996) and 2.5% (registrations with at least 20 inliers).
Registrations supported by fewer than 20 inliers that deviate from the identity by more than 2% in scale or shift or by more than 1 ∘ in rotation are treated as failures, because RANSAC then returns scales between 0.003 and 3.
Such variants are discarded, which affects 2% of the Qwen variants on the neutral floor, 11% on the original floor, 20% of the Kontext and 44% of the LongCat variants.
On real photographs the probe is read in the edited image itself, where the editor’s drift is negligible.
The change mask thresholds the Gaussian-blurred ( σ = 3 \sigma=3 px) absolute grey-level difference at 25 and the blurred ( σ = 5 \sigma=5 px) Laplacian magnitude of the edited image at its median, followed by morphological closing and opening.
The painted region covers 18% of a sharp input and 19–23% of the blurred inputs, i.e . the editor does not re-sharpen the scene.

blocks.en:
Bound on the vanishing points. Tab. S5 compares three bounds on the vanishing points from which the focal length is computed.
The bound of 10 image heights used for the catalog and NYUv2 also caps readable focal lengths at 10 image heights, 240 mm for these frames.
To separate what the read-out can do from what the editor paints, we project an exact board of 12 × 12 12\times 12 tiles into every optical SR-RAW frame with its true focal length and read it with the identical pipeline.
The virtual camera is pitched down so that the horizon lies at least a quarter of the image height above the centre, plus 2–15 ∘ , and the board is rotated by 5–85 ∘ against the view direction.
The exact board passes the image-height bound in only 1 of 12 frames at 240 mm and 6 of 20 at 150 mm, but the scale-free bound in all frames in which it is read at all (8 of 12 and 19 of 20), and it is read with slope 1.00 under every bound (240 mm as 227 mm).
Because the image-height bound discards correct paintings at long focal lengths, it biases the editor’s readable paintings towards too wide perspectives.
For SR-RAW we therefore bound the vanishing points at 10 read-out focal lengths, which requires both line families to be inclined by at least 5.7 ∘ to the image plane.
On the catalog and NYUv2, whose focal lengths stay below 4 image heights, this changes no focal slope by more than 0.05.
Without any bound, estimates from nearly parallel families enter.
The SR-RAW slope with P replace P_{\text{replace}} then rises to 0.69 and the NYUv2 slope with P cover P_{\text{cover}} to 0.30, the Kontext slope on the catalog drops to 0.25, all other slopes change by at most 0.03, and all confidence intervals of the painted boards stay below 1.

为了区分读出能做的和编辑所画的,我们把12×12 12\times 12个瓦片的精确板投射到每个光学SR-RAW相框中,并用相同的管来读取.

准确的取出板只通过12个框架中的1个被捆绑在240毫米,而20个框架中的6个被捆绑在150毫米,但在全部被读取的所有框中(12个框中的8个和20个框中的19个)无比例被捆绑,每个被绑下被用斜坡1.00来读取(240毫米为227毫米).

blocks.en:
We added two open editors, run in ComfyUI with the settings of their model cards and one-megapixel inputs: LongCat-Image-Edit Meituan LongCat Team et al. (2025) (50 steps, guidance 4.5) and OmniGen2 Wu et al. (2026) (50 steps, text guidance 5, image guidance 2), both with one variant per image.
In a smoke test on five catalog renders, LongCat and OmniGen2 each painted a readable board into four.
For lack of compute time, OmniGen2 was then run only for the default camera ( Tab. S3 ).
On the catalog (F ∪ \cup Z, neutral floor), LongCat paints a readable board into 89 of the 120 renders, 58 of them registrable ( Appendix B ).
These do not differ from the others in true roll (median 5.6 ∘ vs . 5.7 ∘ , p = 0.66 p=0.66 , Mann–Whitney) or focal length (31 mm both, p = 0.58 p=0.58 ).
On them, LongCat shows both priors about as strongly as Kontext ( Tab. 2 ), with a roll slope of 0.25 [0.13, 0.36] , a focal slope of 0.34 [0.22, 0.51] and a fixed point of 28 mm.
Unlike Qwen, it also compresses pitch slightly (0.84 [0.66, 0.94] ).
It is the least accurate of the three editors in horizon and pitch ( Tab. 1 ).

blocks.en:
All numbers are computed by scripts from per-image measurements on the lossless editor outputs.
Both main tables and all figures are generated automatically, and measurements, ground truth, renders and JPEG copies of all outputs are archived.
Editing ran on one consumer GPU (median per variant including read-out: 8 s for Qwen with the Lightning distillation, 51 s with the full 40-step model, 73 s for LongCat).
Lightning paints the same perspective as the full model (classroom sweep: focal slopes 0.67 and 0.66, paired focal error not significantly different).
Confidence intervals use 1000 bootstrap resamples over images (2000–4000 for some paired tests), drawn jointly for paired comparisons.
